title: Search API Design
description: Design a search API with full-text search, faceted filtering, pagination, and relevance scoring for product and content discovery.

data.text: Search APIs are the most used endpoints in any product. Users expect instant, relevant results with the ability to filter, sort, and refine. You need a query model that supports full-text search, faceted navigation, and stable pagination across millions of documents.

items: q — free-text query for full-text search
filters — key-value pairs for exact-match faceting
page — cursor token or offset for pagination
fields — sparse fieldsets to control response size

data.title: GET /search?q=wireless+headphones&category=electronics&price_max=200&sort=relevance&limit=20
data.content: Search query with full-text, filters, and cursor pagination.

data.text: Autocomplete is a specialized search endpoint that returns short suggestions as the user types. Use a dedicated endpoint with a low-latency cache (CDN edge or Redis). Debounce client requests to 200-300ms.

data.title: GET /suggest?q=wire&limit=5
data.content: Autocomplete suggestions with result types (product, category, brand).

data.title: Edge caching for search
data.text: Cache search results at the CDN edge using Cache-Control: public, max-age=60. Use stale-while-revalidate to serve slightly stale results while refreshing the cache. Never cache authenticated or personalized search.

items.question: Should I build search on top of my database?
items.answer: Use your database for simple filtering and pagination. Use Elasticsearch or Typesense for full-text search, relevance scoring, and faceted navigation. Mixing both in the same query is a common anti-pattern.

items.question: How do I handle typos in search queries?
items.answer: Enable fuzzy matching (Levenshtein distance 1-2) in your search engine. Combine with n-gram indexing for partial matching. Return a 'Did you mean?' suggestion when the best result relevance is below a threshold.

items.question: What is the best way to paginate deep search results?
items.answer: Use cursor-based pagination with search_after in Elasticsearch. Avoid deep offset pagination (page > 100) as it becomes slow and memory-intensive on the search node.

data.title: Key takeaway
points: Separate full-text search from database filtering; use purpose-built tools.
Cursor pagination is required for stable, high-performance deep results.
Facets enable users to refine queries without typing.
Edge caching makes repeated searches feel instant.
data.takeaway: Search APIs are a product in themselves. Invest in relevance, latency, and discoverability because users judge your entire platform by search quality.
